logistic_regression_baseline: Higher on every metric (98.24% accuracy / 0.9840 F1 / 0.9979 AUC)
lstm: Slightly lower on every metric (97.20% accuracy / 0.9745 F1 / 0.9917 AUC)

logistic_regression_baseline: High - every prediction traces to a signed weight per word (Feature Importance analysis, docs/baseline_model_report.md)
lstm: Low - no per-word coefficients; would need extra techniques (e.g. attention, not implemented) to explain a single prediction
Slow - about 599 seconds (~10 minutes) for the same data; ~2

logistic_regression_baseline: Fast - 0.22 ms/article measured on the test set
lstm: Slower - 1.43 ms/article measured on the test set; ~6.4x slower, though still well within real-time API response budgets

logistic_regression_baseline: Low - trains and predicts on a single CPU core with no special hardware
lstm: Higher - benefits from more CPU/GPU resources; training this run still used CPU-only TensorFlow
Large - ~28.7 MB total (model + tokenizer), roughly 32x bigger

logistic_regression_baseline: 20,001 (one TF-IDF coefficient per vocabulary word, plus intercept)
Scales well computationally, but as a linear model its capacity to keep improving with more data plateaus
lstm: Neural networks typically have more capacity to keep improving as training data grows, though this was not observed on this dataset's current size

logistic_regression_baseline: None - bag-of-words representation cannot distinguish "did not confirm" from "did confirm"
lstm: Structurally capable of using word order, though this dataset did not reward that capability with a higher score

logistic_regression_baseline: Degrades gracefully - a rare word simply gets a small TF-IDF weight
lstm: More fragile - rare/foreign words are more likely to fall outside the 20,000-word cap or have a poorly-learned embedding (see error analysis, docs/lstm_model_report.md)

logistic_regression_baseline: Fully deterministic single solver call - no run-to-run epoch variability to manage
lstm: Visibly noisy training history (validation loss spike at epoch 2, erratic swings at epochs 9-10) - see report/figures/lstm_training_history.png

logistic_regression_baseline: Simple - only needs scikit-learn + joblib at inference time
lstm: Heavier - needs a TensorFlow/Keras runtime, a materially larger dependency footprint

logistic_regression_baseline: Easy to explain, debug, and retrain quickly during development iteration
lstm: Harder to debug (opaque internal state) and slower to iterate on due to long training time

logistic_regression_baseline: Native probability output (predict_proba), used directly for the frontend's confidence display
lstm: Native probability output (sigmoid), equally usable for a confidence display
